local_articles.title: Wimbledon women's draw blasted open as Swiatek and Rybakina crash
local_articles.snippet: LONDON, July 4 - Two gaping holes were blasted into the women's draw at Wimbledonon Saturday as defending champion Iga Swiatek was outplayed by Filipino crowd-pleaser Alexandra Eala and second seed Elena Rybakina was sent packing by Belgian Elise Mertens. Disgruntled Polish third seed Swiatek lost a titanic first-set battle that lasted almost 90 minutes and had no answer to a fearless Eala after that as she lost 7‑6(9) 6-2. Rybakina, the 2022 champion who doubled her Grand Slam tally this year by winning the Australian Open, also fell away badly after a close first set, going down 7-6(4) 6-1 to Mertens who has reached the last 16 for the fourth time. "Definitely I need to analyse and change something, because it's not working," said Rybakina, for whom a run to the quarter-final here could have seen her become world number one. local_articles.title: Alexandra Eala topples holder Iga Swiatek to reach Wimbledon last 16
local_articles.snippet: Iga Swiatek's Wimbledon title defence went up in smoke as the Polish third seed fell 7‑6(9) 6-2 to rising Filipina Alexandra Eala in the third round after a fierce gladiatorial battle at the All England Club on Saturday. Last year's triumph ended years of questions about Swiatek's ability to master the sport's fastest surface, yet the 25-year-old arrived at the All England Club following an early defeat in the Bad Homburg tune-up tournament and still searching for consistency. After battling past Taylor Townsend and sealing an assured win over Karolina Pliskova in her last two rounds, Swiatek came up against an inspired Eala in their Centre Court showdown and fell short under the blazing afternoon sun. local_articles.title: Osaka seeks to break Sabalenka spell as Wimbledon's fourth round begins
local_articles.snippet: LONDON, July 4 - Wimbledon's fourth round begins on Sunday with women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka taking on Naomi Osaka, while men's top seed Jannik Sinner goes up against high-flying Japanese qualifier Shintaro Mochizuki. TOP WOMEN'S MATCH: NAOMI OSAKA V ARYNA SABALENKA Japan's Osaka will be hoping it will be fourth time lucky when she faces Sabalenka, having lost all three of their meetings this year -- at Indian Wells, Madrid and the French Open. Prior to 2026, the pair had not crossed paths for over seven years, with Osaka winning their first-ever clash en route to her maiden Grand Slam triumph at the U.S. Open in 2018. "She's the number one player in the world. If there is someone I had to lose to, I would pick that ranking position," the world number 14 told reporters. "If anything, I would say I learned from all of those matches, so hopefully I can apply (that)." Osaka adde

questions.title: Which Chinese province will evacuate the most people in preparation for Typhoon Bavi by July 11, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Chinese authorities' figures in contemporaneous news coverage. Resolve to the Chinese province with the largest reported number of people evacuated in preparation for Typhoon Bavi as of July 11, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-11 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Notable southward shift in July 3 physical-model guidance narrows Zhejiang's lead and boosts Fujian and Guangdong. Typhoon Bavi explosively intensified on July 3 to Category 5 equivalent (260 km/h, 921 hPa at 12.7N 151.9E east of Guam; CWA upgraded to Strong Typhoon at 20:00 CST with projected 350 km gale radius) and is forecast by CMA, Zhejiang Weather, and CWA to approach Taiwan and China's southeast coast around July 9-11 (closest to Taiwan July 10). Critically, July 3 Taiwanese and Chinese meteorological briefings (NOWnews, TVBS, CNA, NextApple) report a persistent strong subtropical ridge pushing all three major physics/official suites southward toward Taiwan — ECMWF projecting northern Taiwan landfall (which puts both Fujian and southern Zhejiang into massive July 9-11 evacuations, historically favoring Fujian slightly ~62/35 as in Gaemi 2024/Soudelor 2015), GFS projecting a Bashi Channel passage (targeting Guangdong and southern Fujian), and CWA flagging direct Taiwan impact July 10-12 — whereas AI suites (EC-AIFS, Google FNV3, AIGEFS) still favor turning north over waters NE of Taiwan toward the Ryukyus/East China Sea (where Zhejiang dominates pre-emptive evacuations ~70-78% even on offshore near-misses). Blending ~53% Taiwan/Bashi physics tracks and ~47% East China Sea/Ryukyu AI tracks trims Zhejiang from 0.50 to 0.45 (still #1 via East China Sea dominance plus large northern-Taiwan spillover), lifts Fujian from 0.32 to 0.35, lifts Guangdong sharply from 0.05 to 0.11 (overtaking Shanghai on the GFS Bashi Channel scenario), and trims Shanghai (0.06 -> 0.04) and Jiangsu (0.03 -> 0.02), leaving 0.03 tail for Shandong/other/far-east recurve.

local_articles.title: Super Typhoon Bavi Approaches US Pacific Islands, Could Strike Monday
local_articles.snippet: People in Guam and the Northern Marianas readied themselves on Saturday as the second "super typhoon" since April drew closer to the US territories, bringing the equivalent of category-5 hurricane winds. Bavi was moving westward with sustained winds of 269 kilometres per hour (167 miles per hour) and gusts of 324 kph (201 mph), the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) said in an update at 7:00 pm local time (0900 GMT). The eye of the storm was expected to pass on Monday very close to the small island of Rota between Guam and Saipan, the main island of the Northern Marianas, with winds set to strengthen to 278 kph, the JTWC forecast. local_articles.title: Super Typhoon Bavi heads for US Pacific islands
local_articles.snippet: SAIPAN, Northern Mariana Islands – People in Guam and the Northern Marianas hunkered down on July 4 as the second super typhoon to hit the US Pacific territories since April approached with the equivalent of Category 5 hurricane winds. Bavi was several hundred kilometres east of the archipelago with sustained winds of 259kmh, and gusts of 314kmh, the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) said in an update at 7am Guam time (5am Singapore time). “Current forecast tracks continue to indicate a grim outlook for the Marianas,” the US National Weather Service warned. “All residents across Guam and the (Northern Mariana Islands) should plan for and anticipate at least tropical storm conditions.” The islands’ roughly 200,000 inhabitants have queued at petrol stations in recent days and thronged hardware stores to buy plywood and supermarkets for food, bottled water and other essentials. questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 3 model shift flips Fujian ahead of Zhejiang as #1 first-landfall favorite and lifts Guangdong sharply. On July 3, Typhoon Bavi explosively reached Category 5 equivalent (260 km/h, 921 hPa at 12.7N 151.9E) moving west under a very strong subtropical ridge, with CMA and Taiwan CWA projecting approach to Taiwan and China's eastern sea around July 10. Crucially, July 3 briefings (NOWnews, TVBS, CNA, NextApple) report a sharp physics-vs-AI bifurcation: ECMWF targets northern Taiwan landfall, GFS sends Bavi even further south through the Bashi Channel, and CWA projects Taiwan landfall/impact July 10-12, while AI suites (EC-AIFS, Google FNV3, AIGEFS) favor recurving NE of Taiwan toward the Ryukyus/East China Sea. Because this question is strictly conditional on a qualifying mainland China landfall (void if Bavi recurves cleanly into Okinawa/Japan/Korea), Bayes' rule strips out non-landfalling AI recurves and heavily weights the physics/Taiwan-corridor scenarios: typhoons crossing northern/central Taiwan on a WNW heading hit Fujian first ~74% of the time vs southern Zhejiang ~22% (analogues: Gaemi 2024, Maria 2018, Dujuan/Soudelor 2015, Nepartak 2016), while Bashi Channel tracks (GFS) split ~55% Guangdong / ~42% southern Fujian. Across our 4-regime conditional landfall model, Fujian surges +0.085 (0.38 -> 0.465) into #1, Zhejiang drops -0.105 (0.42 -> 0.315, relying on East China Sea tracks curving west plus northern-Taiwan NW bends), Guangdong jumps +0.065 (0.08 -> 0.145), and Shanghai (0.030) and Jiangsu (0.025) trim slightly, leaving 0.020 for Shandong/Liaoning/Hainan/Guangxi.
